_scenario: One §36 ParticleEmitter (maxParticles 100, seed 1337, a 40-particle burst at t=0 plus 90 particles/s, lifetimes 0.8–2 s, a 0.55 rad cone at 2–5 units/s, size and RGBA ramps) under four §27 fields applied in declaration order — uniform gravity (0,−9.81,0), linear drag 0.4, a vortex about +Y (strength 3, minDistance 0.25) and a seeded turbulence field (seed 4242, amplitude 2.5, frequency 0.8) — bouncing off §36's collision plane at y = −1.5 with restitution 0.45. The emitter is stepped by a ParticleSystem registered on the Application's §39 registry at priority 500; a ParticleRenderable repacks the instance array every step. fixedTimeStep 1/60, 600 clean injected frames (10 s, exactly one fixed step each, nothing dropped). FNV-1a per D6 with 1e-6 quantization over the whole live pool after every step: the live count plus each particle's position (3), velocity (3), age, lifetime, size endpoints (2) and colour endpoints (8), in slot order. The pool saturates, so 213 of 940 spawns are dropped — which is what pins maxParticles as part of the determinism contract.
_tier: same-runtime (§33): the seeded stream, the ascending-index iteration, the swap-remove compaction, the field summation order and the checksum are all exact and cross-platform, but the inputs are runtime-bound — the spawn cone calls Math.cos/Math.sin, the vortex and turbulence fields call Math.sqrt/Math.floor, and every pool channel is a Float32Array.
